stories.headline: US Air Force pulls bombers from UK air base after suspected terror attack
stories.title: US Air Force pulls bombers from UK air base after suspected terror attack
stories.summary: The US Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a US-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base. The bombers were redeployed back to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorized to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke Sunday on condition of anonymity. Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers fly out of the base on Sunday. The move comes as President Donald Trump weighs options for his war on Iran - including new strikes - despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks. "We have decisions that I'll make about Iran. Iran's been decimated. So the only question is - it'll either be the easy way, or the hard way,"

stories.headline: India seeks bigger role in effort to end the Russia-Ukraine War
stories.title: India seeks bigger role in effort to end the Russia-Ukraine War
stories.summary: The comments point to a more active role for New Delhi after years of taking a cautious approach to the war, in part because of its longstanding ties with Russia
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: India is taking a more direct role in efforts to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, engaging both sides on issues, including shipping and reducing hostilities, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said.

Speaking at a security conference over the weekend, Jaishankar said India in recent months has become “a little bit more involved beyond advocacy.” The comments point to a more active role for New Delhi after years of taking a cautious approach to the war, in part because of its longstanding ties with Russia.
“We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.
We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” he said, adding that talks have also covered energy shipments and “non-attack possibilities.”
India has called for a halt to the fighting but has been reluctant to criticize the Kremlin, abstaining from United Nations votes condemning the war.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the conflict during a meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan in late August.
Jaishankar said dialogue and diplomacy are essential to ending the war.
He added that India’s relationship with Russia has evolved over the years and now spans energy, space and trade.

When Modi met Putin on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in September, the two pledged to deepen ties, underscoring their close relationship even as Washington pressed New Delhi to distance itself from Moscow.
The US has sought to use its position as India’s top trading partner to pressure New Delhi to stop buying Russian oil.
India’s purchases initially declined before picking up again during the Middle East war.
Russia is also a major supplier of weapons to New Delhi.

stories.headline: Magnitude 3.8 Earthquake Strikes Tripura's Dhalai District, No Damage Reported
stories.title: Magnitude 3.8 Earthquake Strikes Tripura's Dhalai District, No Damage Reported
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: AGARTALA: An earthquake of magnitude 3.8 on the Richter scale struck the Dhalai district of Tripura in the early hours of Sunday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
As per data shared by the nodal agency, the tremors were recorded at 00:57:38 IST at a depth of 30 kilometres.
The epicentre was determined at Latitude 23.757 N and Longitude 91.995 E in Dhalai.

"EQ of M: 3.8, On: 04/10/2026 00:57:38 IST, Lat: 23.757 N, Long: 91.995 E, Depth: 30 Km, Location: Dhalai, Tripura," the National Center for Seismology posted on X. No immediate reports of casualties or damage to property have been received so far.

stories.title: Brazil election: Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro head to runoff after tight first-round vote
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face each other in a runoff election. Neither candidate obtained the majority required during the first round of voting. The runoff election is scheduled for October 25, 2026, with major issues such as corruption and cost of living impacting the campaign. Both candidates are expected to appeal to voters from eliminated candidates.

stories.headline: RBI may end rate-cut cycle with first hike since February 2023
stories.title: RBI may end rate-cut cycle with first hike since February 2023
stories.summary: Bankers expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points soon. This marks the end of the rate-cutting phase that began in February 2025. Economists predict inflation will exceed the RBI’s forecasts, necessitating tightening. Experts anticipate resilient growth will provide the RBI room to act despite external pressures. The focus will remain on managing liquidity and aligning rates with policy measures.

stories.headline: Assam Cabinet approves Rs 3,000 green cess on transfer of vehicles over 3 years old
stories.title: Assam Cabinet approves Rs 3,000 green cess on transfer of vehicles over 3 years old
stories.summary: The green cess will, however, not apply to EVs, CNG vehicles, two- and three-wheelers and transfer of ownership owing to death of vehicle owner.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Guwahati: In a major development, the State Cabinet under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma on Sunday decided to reserve 12% of constable posts in Assam.
Police, Fire Brigade, State Disaster Response Force, and Prison, Forest and Excise departments for ex-Agniveers of Indian Army.
Announcing this, Sarma told the media that the former Agniveers should however be permanent residents of Assam to avail benefit of the reservation.
He said this was part of a nationwide policy, so that after four years of serving the army as Agniveers, they can work in their respective states.
He mentioned that as the Agniveers are already trained, their services will strengthen the government agencies that recruit them.
The cabinet also cleared a Rs 10,200 crore investment proposal from Dalmia Bharat Cement for setting up a cement plant in the state.
According to the chief minister, a memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed between the state overnment and the company during Advantage Assam 2.0 held in Guwahati in February 2025.
Meanwhile, the National Highway (NH) part was bifurcated from the NH & Building wing of Public Works Department (PWD) and merged with PWD Roads.
A decision to this effect was taken by the cabinet, which also approved creation of a commissioner's post to oversee the functioning of the newly-created PWD Roads & NH division.
In another major decision, the cabinet also waved green cess of transfer of ownership of electric vehicles, CNG vehicles, and two and three wheelers.
Sarma elaborated that if a vehicle owner dies, the nominees operating such classes of vehicles too would not have to pay the green cess.
But, he emphasised that all other category of vehicles older than three years would have to pay a green cess of Rs 3,000 while resale.
